concepts.title: Area Under a Curve (x-axis)
concepts.definition: The total area bounded by a function y=f(x), the x-axis, and vertical lines x=a and x=b is calculated by integrating the function with respect to x over the interval [a, b].
concepts.key_idea: Summation of infinite vertical strips of height y and width dx.
question_patterns: find the area bounded by the curve
calculate the area under the function
what is the area enclosed by the curve and x-axis
determine the area between the ordinates
Explain the method of Area Under a Curve (x-axis).

solution_steps.explain: Set up the definite integral of the function f(x) from a to b.
Compute the antiderivative F(x) of f(x) with respect to x to prepare for applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

solution_steps.action: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
solution_steps.explain: Evaluate F(b) - F(a) to obtain the numerical value of the definite integral representing the enclosed area.

concepts.title: Area Under a Curve (y-axis)
concepts.definition: The area bounded by a curve x=g(y), the y-axis, and horizontal lines y=c and y=d is found by integrating the function with respect to y.
concepts.key_idea: Summation of infinite horizontal strips of width x and height dy.
question_patterns: find the area bounded by the curve and y-axis
calculate the area using horizontal strips
what is the area between lines y=c and y=d
determine the area enclosed by x=g(y)
Explain the method of Area Under a Curve (y-axis).

solution_steps.explain: Set up the definite integral of the function g(y) from c to d.
Compute the antiderivative G(y) of g(y) with respect to y to prepare for applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

solution_steps.action: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
solution_steps.explain: Evaluate G(d) - G(c) to obtain the numerical value of the definite integral representing the enclosed area.

concepts.title: Absolute Area for Negative Regions
concepts.definition: When a curve lies below the x-axis, the definite integral yields a negative value; the actual geometric area is the absolute value of this integral.
concepts.key_idea: Geometric area must always be non-negative.
question_patterns: find the total area bounded by the curve
calculate the area considering portions below x-axis
what is the absolute area enclosed by the curve
how to handle negative integral values for area
Explain the method of Absolute Area for Negative Regions.

solution_steps.explain: Calculate the definite integral over the interval.
Ensure the final area is positive.
The absolute value ensures the area is non-negative regardless of whether the curve lies above or below the x-axis.
